candidate.selection_reason: cookie string input -> slice operation based on regex match -> modifies cookie parsing behavior
candidate.source_summary: str is the input cookie string, trimmed. It may come from external sources (e.g., HTTP Set-Cookie header). The TRAILING_SEMICOLON regex /;+$/ matches one or more semicolons at the end of the string.
candidate.sink_summary: The transformed str is further parsed to extract cookie key, value, and attributes (expires, domain, path, secure, httponly, extensions). The resulting Cookie object may be stored and later used for HTTP requests, affecting authentication, session management, and security policies.
candidate.guard_summary: If strict mode is true, the function returns early (line 308) and does not slice. The slice only occurs when strict is false. The slice uses semiColonCheck.index, which is the position of the first semicolon in the trailing sequence, effectively removing all trailing semicolons. Subsequent parsing uses regexes (COOKIE_PAIR or COOKIE_PAIR_STRICT) and validation steps (parseDate, domain canonicalization, path checks) that may reject malformed inputs.
candidate.risk_pattern: In non‑strict mode, trailing semicolons are stripped before parsing. If an attacker crafts a cookie string with embedded semicolons that are not at the very end, they may be interpreted as attribute separators, potentially altering the cookie’s domain, path, secure flag, or extensions. The slice operation could also affect the parsing of the name‑value pair if the regex matching is misaligned.
candidate.context_summary: The parse function is the main cookie‑parsing routine per RFC 6265. The changed line removes trailing semicolons only when strict=false. This is a relaxation of the spec (S4.1.1) that may allow non‑conforming cookie strings to be accepted and parsed differently than in strict mode.

target_cwe.description: Authenticating a user, or otherwise establishing a new user session, without invalidating any existing session identifier gives an attacker the opportunity to steal authenticated sessions.
remediation_steps: Implement proper authentication and session management

stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: Cookie parsing vulnerability could enable session manipulation through attribute injection
